notes: Parameters of published silicon two-qubit devices. Units are in the parameter names. 'assumed': false means the number is printed in the cited version of the paper ('values_from'). 'assumed': true entries carry a 'basis' (derived from reported numbers, assumed typical value, lower bound or upper bound) and a one-line 'reason'. Per-qubit values are [Q1, Q2].

ramsey_averaging_s.reason: Ramsey averaging time not reported. It sets the low cut-off of the 1/f^alpha spectrum that is pinned to the quasi-static width: for alpha = 1 only through a logarithm, but where alpha is fitted it moves the fitted exponent (Mills Q2 1.63 to 1.37, Tanttu 1.23 to 1.12, for 10 s to 1 h) while the CZ totals change by less than 0.4%.

zeeman_alpha.reason: Used only for qubits without a reported echo time; otherwise the exponent is fitted per qubit to T2* and the Hahn-echo time.

exchange_alpha.reason: 1/f spectrum for delta J / J above the Ramsey band; no paper here gives an exchange-noise spectrum to fit.

reported_error_budget.source: Xue 2022, Extended Data Table 1, Methods 'CZ gate' and 'Gate set tomography'

gst_cz_coherent_infidelity.reason: (d/(d+1)) theta_J^2 = 0.8 x 0.016^2, the coherent part of the average infidelity; the stochastic part is 0.8 x 0.0042 = 3.36e-3.

authors_simulated_infidelity.source: Xue 2022, Methods, 'CZ gate' (average gate infidelity 1 - F = 0.22e-3 with noise, < 1e-6 without). Their simulation takes delta f_Q1, delta f_Q2 as quasi-static and delta v_B as 1/f noise, and includes the barrier-voltage dependence of the qubit frequencies (beta_1, beta_2), which this model leaves out

recalibration_interval_h.source: Xue 2022, Methods, 'Gate calibration' (qubit frequencies recalibrated by Ramsey sequences every 2 h, at the start and in the middle of the GST run)

benchmark_duration_h.source: Xue 2022, Methods, 'Gate calibration' (Ramsey recalibration 'every 2 h, at the beginning and in the middle' of the GST experiment)
benchmark_duration_h.reason: A recalibration at the start and one in the middle, 2 h apart, puts the GST run at about 4 h; the run length is not printed. The methods describe no recalibration of J during the run, so exchange drift is taken over the whole run.

drift_j_rel_per_sqrt_h.source: not reported in Xue 2022; used only by the recalibration estimate
drift_j_rel_per_sqrt_h.reason: Random-walk rate of J; the same size as the quasi-static dJ/J = 0.97% fitted over 8-minute averages. The authors attribute their excess error to slower barrier drift but give no rate.

drift_dez_mhz_per_sqrt_h.source: not reported in Xue 2022; used only by the recalibration estimate
drift_dez_mhz_per_sqrt_h.reason: Random-walk rate of the frequency difference; of the order of the 11 and 24 kHz quasi-static widths fitted over 8-minute averages. With independent qubit drift (the default) each qubit frequency walks at 1/sqrt(2) of this, about 14 kHz/sqrt(h).

calibration_std_j_rel.source: not reported in Xue 2022; used only by the recalibration estimate
calibration_std_j_rel.reason: Relative error of J from one exchange-oscillation (conditional-phase) fit; typical for a few hundred shots per point.

calibration_std_dez_mhz.source: not reported in Xue 2022; used only by the recalibration estimate
calibration_std_dez_mhz.reason: Error of the frequency difference from the Ramsey fits, a few kHz for T2* = 10-20 us. With independent qubit drift (the default) each qubit frequency is taken to be measured to 1/sqrt(2) of this, about 3.5 kHz.

exchange_sigma_rel.source: Noiri 2022, Extended Data Fig. 5a caption ('Single-qubit frequency noises (Delta f1 and Delta f2) are larger than that of the exchange noise Delta J/2') and main text (T2* 'mostly limited by single-qubit frequency noise')
exchange_sigma_rel.reason: Delta J/2 < Delta f, with Delta f at most the conditional Ramsey width sqrt(2)/(2 pi T2*) = 31.9 kHz for Q1 (T2* = 7.05 us), gives Delta J < 64 kHz, i.e. delta J/J < 0.34% at J = 18.85 MHz; this bound is used. It is not tight: if the conditional width is the quadrature sum of Delta f and Delta J/2, the same statement gives Delta J < sqrt(2) x 31.9 kHz, i.e. 0.24%.
